New York Pizza Dough

Stretch a larger ball so the center is thin and the rim is modest. Bake it hot on a stone or steel if you have one. Start with 4 balls at 400 g, a full New York round each. Type a different count when you want more or fewer pies.

Detailed method

The calculator opens at 4 balls of 400 g, with 63% hydration, 2.2% salt, and 0.25% yeast. Each ball is one large round. From those balls the page shows 967.1 g flour, 609.2 g water, 21.3 g salt, and 2.4 g yeast. Sauce and cheese are extra and are not in the gram total. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Mix Stir 967.1 g flour, 609.2 g water, and 2.4 g instant yeast until no dry flour remains, then work in 21.3 g salt. At 63% the dough is soft, and a little firmer than a wetter pizza dough. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  2. Rest Cover the bowl and leave it for 20 minutes so the dough stops tearing when you fold it.
  3. Bulk Keep it covered at about 24°C (75°F) for 60 to 90 minutes. Give it one stretch-and-fold halfway through. It should look a little puffier, not doubled. With 0.25% yeast, most of the rise happens later in the cold.
  4. Ball Divide into 4 balls of 400 g, the count and the weight the page opens with. Tighten each one so the skin is smooth. Set them in a covered tray with a little space between them.
  5. Cold ferment Refrigerate the balls at about 4°C (39°F) for 16 to 24 hours. They should spread slightly and smell mildly yeasty.
  6. Warm and stretch Take the balls out 60 to 90 minutes before baking. Stretch each one by hand on a floured peel to about 32 cm. Keep the center thin and the rim modest. Avoid a rolling pin, because it presses out the air bubbles and makes the crust tough.
  7. Top and bake Heat a stone or steel at 250°C (480°F), or as hot as the oven will go, for 45 minutes. Spread about 70 g of sauce and 90 g of cheese on each round. Those toppings are extra and are not in the gram total. Bake 8 to 12 minutes, until the rim is spotted and the center is set.
  8. Rest Set the pizza on a rack for 2 minutes before you cut it, so a slice can hold.
